articles.title: Skyline Social Partners with Intercard for 100,000 Sq Ft Minnesota FEC
articles.summary: Intercard's cashless technology has been selected to power the arcade at Skyline Social & Games in Apple Valley, Minnesota, a sprawling 100,000 sq ft indoor-outdoor family entertainment center operated by the Kolquist family. The venue represents a significant new FEC opening in the Midwest, combining games with a broad entertainment mix. The deal highlights how established bowling operators are expanding into full FEC formats with modern cashless infrastructure.

articles.title: Semnox and Texas FEC Lumos Build Custom RFID Redemption Integration
articles.summary: Semnox Solutions has partnered with Lumos, a Texas entertainment venue featuring bowling, arcade, axe-throwing, and laser tag, to develop a bespoke RFID cashless and redemption system that goes beyond off-the-shelf solutions. The custom Parafait integration connects Semnox's cashless platform with Lumos's proprietary redemption system, reducing guest and staff friction since the venue's October 2025 opening. This case study is directly relevant to FEC operators evaluating how far they can push cashless technology customization.

articles.title: Semnox Parafait RFID System Powers Multi-Attraction Texas Venue Lumos
articles.summary: InPark Magazine covers the same Semnox-Lumos partnership, detailing how the RFID cashless system spans the arcade and all attractions at Lumos since its October 2025 launch. The custom integration gives FEC operators a real-world example of unified technology infrastructure across diverse attraction types. Operators considering cashless upgrades should note the bespoke redemption angle as a competitive differentiator.

articles.title: Lucky Strike Entertainment Posts $1.25B Revenue in FY2026 with Narrow Loss
articles.summary: Lucky Strike Entertainment Corp reported full-year 2026 revenue of $1.25 billion alongside an EPS loss of $0.33 in its 10-K filing, offering a rare public financial benchmark for the bowling and entertainment center sector. The results reflect the scale achievable by large FEC operators running bowling-anchored social entertainment venues. Investors and operators tracking the industry's financial health will find this a useful data point for benchmarking.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia Accelerates $13.3 Billion Indoor Entertainment Center Buildout
articles.summary: Saudi Arabia is intensifying its massive investment in indoor entertainment centers as part of Vision 2030 leisure development goals, with the total buildout now valued at $13.3 billion. This represents a substantial global opportunity for FEC suppliers, ride manufacturers, and attraction technology companies seeking international growth. Operators and investors should monitor Saudi Arabia as one of the world's fastest-growing markets for FEC-style venues.

articles.title: accesso's Lee Cowie on AI, Data, and the Future of Attractions Technology
articles.summary: accesso's feature in InPark Magazine explores how AI and data analytics are pushing ticketing and in-park purchasing well beyond traditional transaction processing, with the goal of removing every obstacle between guest and experience. For FEC operators, the insight that frictionless purchasing directly drives spend-per-visit is highly actionable. The piece signals where leading attractions technology vendors are investing their R&D for the near term.

articles.title: InPark Issue 111 Editorial: Frictionless Guest Experience as the North Star
articles.summary: InPark Magazine's publisher Martin Palicki argues that removing friction from every guest touchpoint — ticketing, purchasing, and in-park navigation — should be the defining design principle for attractions operators today. The editorial frames the broader theme of the magazine's 111th issue, which covers AI, interactive storytelling, and inclusive design. FEC operators will find this a useful strategic lens for evaluating technology investments.

articles.title: Texas' Largest Family Entertainment Center Opens in Houston in 2026
articles.summary: A venue billing itself as Texas's biggest family entertainment center has opened in Houston in 2026, signaling continued appetite for large-format FEC development in major metro markets. The opening adds competitive pressure on existing operators in the Houston area and reflects the ongoing trend toward destination-scale entertainment complexes. FEC operators in similar markets should take note of the format and scope.

articles.title: $50M EVO Entertainment Destination Clears Site in Downtown Clearwater
articles.summary: A $50 million EVO Entertainment complex has cleared its site in downtown Clearwater, Florida, marking a significant step toward one of the larger urban FEC developments currently underway in the Southeast. EVO's model combines cinema, bowling, gaming, and dining, making it a direct competitor to standalone FEC operators in the region. The project underscores the trend of entertainment anchors replacing traditional retail in downtown corridors.

articles.title: Launch Family Fun Center Adding Arcade and Trampoline Park to Pensacola Market
articles.summary: Launch Family Fun Center is bringing a combined arcade and trampoline park to Davis Highway in Pensacola, Florida, expanding the brand's footprint in the Southeast. The opening adds a new competitive option for family entertainment in a mid-size market that has seen growing demand for experiential leisure. Trampoline park and arcade operators monitoring regional expansion trends will want to track this development.

articles.title: Mr Gatti's Targets Lubbock Franchise Return with New FEC Opportunity
articles.summary: Mr Gatti's, the entertainment-dining brand, is looking at re-entering the Lubbock, Texas market through a new family entertainment center franchise opportunity. The move reflects a broader resurgence of entertainment-dining franchise models seeking suburban and secondary market locations. Prospective FEC franchisees and multi-unit operators should monitor Mr Gatti's updated concept as a potential investment vehicle.

articles.title: Major Kansas City Entertainment Center Closes After 13 Years
articles.summary: A large family entertainment center in Kansas City has shut its doors after 13 years of operation, highlighting the ongoing challenges facing independently operated FEC venues in competitive urban markets. The closure leaves a notable gap in the local market and raises questions about what combination of attractions and business model changes could succeed at the site. FEC operators and investors should study the factors behind the closure as a cautionary case study.

articles.title: Jora Vision Expands into Competitive Socializing with New Interactive Portfolio
articles.summary: Jora Vision is growing its competitive socializing offering, positioning the design firm as a key supplier for FEC operators looking to add skill-based group entertainment experiences. The feature in InPark highlights how competitive socializing continues to evolve beyond simple darts and bowling lanes into more elaborate interactive formats. FEC operators designing new venues or refreshing existing ones should evaluate Jora Vision's expanding capability set.

articles.title: Six Flags and Warner Bros. Invest in Premium Interactive Horror Experience for Halloween
articles.summary: Six Flags, Plague Productions, and Warner Bros. Discovery Global Experiences have collaborated on The Conjuring: Beyond Fear, a premium interactive horror experience designed to drive upsell revenue during the critical fall season. The InPark feature examines how operators can move large Halloween crowds efficiently while still delivering high-yield premium experiences. FEC and theme park operators running Halloween events will find practical takeaways on monetizing the season.

articles.title: Alton Towers Adds Immersive Story-Driven Dining to Halloween Scarefest 2026
articles.summary: Alton Towers is launching Dine with the Dead, a three-act immersive dining experience for Scarefest 2026, marking the resort's first foray into story-driven dinner entertainment within its Halloween event. The experience blends cocktail reception, three-course dining, and an afterparty with live theatrical performance, creating a premium upsell layer over the standard event ticket. FEC and attraction operators running Halloween programming should note this as a model for adding high-margin experiential dining to seasonal events.

articles.title: How to Choose and Budget for the Right Trade Association for Your Attractions Business
articles.summary: Blooloop's two-part guide helps attractions operators and suppliers evaluate which industry associations deliver genuine ROI beyond the annual trade show floor, focusing on mission alignment, workforce credentials, market intelligence, and advocacy value. The piece is especially timely as FEC operators weigh memberships in bodies like IAAPA, BALPPA, or niche regional groups with limited budgets. A practical read for any operator making membership decisions heading into the new fiscal year.

articles.title: Chuck E. Cheese Runs Month-Long Fundraiser for American Society for Deaf Children
articles.summary: Chuck E. Cheese has launched a month-long fundraising campaign in honor of National Deaf Awareness Month, benefiting the American Society for Deaf Children. The initiative demonstrates how large FEC brands can use cause marketing to deepen community ties and drive in-venue traffic during a typically slower period. Operators looking to build inclusive brand identity and local goodwill should consider similar accessibility-focused partnerships.

articles.title: New Family Entertainment Center Opening in Rock Springs, Wyoming
articles.summary: A new family entertainment center is set to open in Rock Springs, Wyoming, bringing structured indoor family entertainment to a smaller market that has limited existing options. The opening reflects the continued geographic spread of FEC formats beyond major metros into secondary and tertiary markets. Developers and franchisors targeting underserved markets should monitor smaller-market openings like this as proof-of-concept signals.

articles.title: Mr. Putters Expands Indoor Mini Golf Entertainment Across Tampa Bay
articles.summary: Mr. Putters is expanding its indoor entertainment offerings for families, schools, and corporate clients throughout the Tampa Bay region, growing its reach beyond a single location. The expansion highlights mini golf as a durable FEC anchor attraction with broad demographic appeal and strong group booking potential. Operators evaluating low-footprint, high-appeal attraction additions should look at indoor mini golf's continued growth trajectory.

articles.title: Endless Surf and Flowstate Partner to Bring AI Vision Technology to Surf Parks
articles.summary: Endless Surf and Flowstate have announced a strategic partnership combining customizable wave technology with AI-powered computer vision to create a more connected and personalized experience for surf park guests and operators. The Mixtape integration delivers real-time performance data and personalization, pushing surf parks further into the experiential technology space. FEC investors and operators tracking emerging attraction categories should watch surf parks as a potential premium addition to large-format venues.

articles.title: Citysaurus AI Photo Souvenir Platform Reaches 50th Location Milestone
articles.summary: Amsterdam-based Citysaurus has opened its 50th AI-powered photobooth location, reflecting rapid growth of its souvenir technology platform across museums, visitor attractions, and immersive venues since 2021. The company's system offers a space-efficient, high-margin ancillary revenue solution that could fit well in FEC environments where floor space is at a premium. Operators looking to boost per-visit spend with low-footprint tech should evaluate AI souvenir kiosks as a category.

articles.title: Lake Compounce Names Daniel LLanas as New General Manager
articles.summary: Lake Compounce, America's oldest amusement park, has appointed Daniel LLanas as General Manager, bringing over 25 years of theme park, water park, and destination attraction leadership experience to the role. Leadership transitions at established regional parks often signal strategic shifts in operations, marketing, or capital investment. Operators and suppliers with relationships at the park should take note of the new point of contact.

articles.title: Alterface Marks 25 Years of Interactive Attraction Design
articles.summary: Alterface, a leading designer of interactive dark rides and shooting experiences, is celebrating its 25th anniversary with a retrospective on how the company has shaped interactive themed entertainment worldwide. For FEC operators considering interactive dark rides or shooting galleries as anchor attractions, Alterface's portfolio and philosophy offer relevant design and procurement insights. The anniversary feature also previews where the company is heading with next-generation interactivity.

articles.title: Long Beach Island Drugstore to Be Converted into Family Entertainment Center
articles.summary: A long-vacant drugstore on Long Beach Island, New Jersey, is being redeveloped into a family entertainment center, illustrating the ongoing conversion of shuttered retail into experiential leisure destinations. The project follows a well-established post-pandemic pattern of FEC operators targeting affordable, high-visibility retail vacancies in tourist-adjacent areas. Developers and franchisors scouting adaptive reuse opportunities should monitor this type of conversion activity.

articles.title: Korea's 9.81 Park Partners with Paradise City Resort Ahead of Incheon Airport Opening
articles.summary: DSM's 9.81 Park, an AI-enhanced gravity racing and experiential leisure park, has signed a joint marketing agreement with the Paradise City integrated resort ahead of its new Incheon Airport location opening next spring. The Incheon venue will be roughly twice the size of the original Jeju location, targeting over one million annual visitors. FEC operators and investors interested in tech-forward competitive attractions and Asian market growth should track 9.81 Park's expansion.

articles.title: Fresno Bed Bath & Beyond Converted to Indoor Entertainment Venue
articles.summary: A former Bed Bath & Beyond store in Fresno, California is being transformed into an indoor entertainment destination, continuing the national trend of large-format retail vacancies being repurposed for family entertainment. The conversion gives FEC operators in secondary California markets a new local competitor to be aware of. For developers, this is another data point supporting the viability of big-box retail conversion as an FEC real estate strategy.

articles.title: Chance Rides Launches All-Electric Utility eTRAM for Attractions Operations
articles.summary: Chance Rides has introduced the Utility eTRAM, an all-electric vehicle built for maintenance and facilities teams at theme parks, resorts, zoos, and large entertainment venues to move equipment and supplies with zero emissions. The product addresses a growing need for sustainable behind-the-scenes logistics as attractions operators face environmental and operational efficiency pressures. FEC operators running large campuses or planning green initiatives should evaluate electric utility vehicles as part of their infrastructure planning.

articles.title: Inclusion and Accessibility Are Good for FEC Business, Advocates Argue
articles.summary: InPark Magazine's ongoing series with the Big Break Foundation makes the business case that diversity, equity, inclusion, and accessibility initiatives are not just ethical obligations but revenue drivers for attractions operators. For FEC operators, accessible design and inclusive programming can meaningfully expand the addressable guest base while strengthening community relationships. The column offers a practical framing that operators can use when pitching accessibility investments internally.
